title: European tour and playing with Duke Ellington's band
summary: The Kid Thomas band toured Europe and shared bills with Ellington.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: What was the first time I went to?
I went to, what was it, my first time?

Oh, sure. I know we went up, went over to Europe. We went around near Belgium, went to England, and we went somewhere in Italy. Somewhere in Belgium was like a big place. You know, one place was behind the Iron Curtain, or something like that. But the woman that sang, was singing with Duke Ellington. She requested to sing Coastal Walk with us. And people that were promoting that asked for Duke Ellington and Count Basie, I mean Duke Ellington, and the Cuttombs Band to play together. And I was honored when Duke Ellington could accept the invitation and ask for him to play whatever he wanted. What I'm saying is to show you how powerful, or how much drawn attraction this old, traditional music is compared to those other kinds of musicians. We traveled good. What is Japan together? Yeah. So we got just as much recognition as they got. They had a saxophone player with Duke. He was an alcoholic. He was a problem. And Duke, I would talk to them, because I knew Kool-Aid very well, because he was Mobile. I understand that. But this guy, all bands have strict rules. I care how much he'd drink, Duke had a slow, remember the song in the slow tempo, and he had one in the fast tempo. And that guy, he was drunk. But Duke had an order in this band, I was told, that if you're sore as you get drunk, but if you can't do your solo and things like that, then you go. But out of watching, he would never miss nothing. When you're playing in slow tempo, and you're doing all that vibration, you kind of get tricky and meaner and look what the next ball is.
Then he had his fast song. He'd never miss it.

Because he knew, he knew, the rules and the recreation of the band, which goes with all bands, all organizations. And we got to be close friends after they found out that we could draw as much as they draw, as much as they draw, and we did. And it even amazes me.
